title: Mars-1: Exploring the Red Planet
description: Discover Mars, its landscape, missions, and the search for past life.

questions.question: What is Mars commonly called?
questions.explain: Iron-rich dust gives Mars its reddish appearance.

questions.question: Which planet is Mars from the Sun?
questions.explain: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.

questions.question: What is the name of Mars's largest volcano?
questions.explain: Olympus Mons is a huge shield volcano.

questions.question: Mars has two small natural moons.
questions.explain: Its moons are Phobos and Deimos.

questions.question: What are the names of Mars's two moons?
questions.explain: Phobos and Deimos are named after figures associated with fear and terror in Greek mythology.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of Mars's atmosphere?
questions.explain: Mars's thin atmosphere is mostly carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Mars is warmer than Earth on average.
questions.explain: Mars is much colder than Earth on average.

questions.question: What is the name of the large canyon system on Mars?
questions.explain: Valles Marineris stretches thousands of kilometers across Mars.

questions.question: What is the name of NASA's rover that landed on Mars in 2021?
questions.explain: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater in February 2021.

questions.question: Which NASA rover landed on Mars in 2012?
questions.explain: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater in August 2012.

questions.question: Liquid water currently flows widely across the surface of Mars.
questions.explain: Stable liquid water is not known to flow widely on the present-day surface.

questions.question: Why do scientists study ancient river channels and lakebeds on Mars?
options: To learn whether Mars once had conditions suitable for life
questions.explain: Past water environments help scientists investigate whether Mars could once have supported microbial life.

questions.question: What is the name of the first artificial object to reach Mars successfully?
questions.explain: NASA's Mariner 4 flew past Mars in 1965 and returned the first close-up images.

questions.question: Humans have already walked on Mars.
questions.explain: No human has visited Mars yet; robotic spacecraft have explored it.

questions.question: What is a Martian day called?
questions.explain: A sol is one rotation of Mars, about 24 hours and 39 minutes.

questions.question: What is the name of the enormous impact basin where Perseverance landed?
questions.explain: Jezero Crater once contained a lake and river delta.

questions.question: Which color best describes the sky near the Martian surface during daytime?
questions.explain: Fine dust often makes the daytime sky look butterscotch-colored; sunsets can appear bluish near the Sun.

questions.question: Mars has seasons because its axis is tilted.
questions.explain: Mars's axial tilt causes seasonal changes, much like Earth's.

questions.question: What is the main goal of searching for signs of ancient life on Mars?
options: To prove aliens live there today
To learn whether life ever existed beyond Earth
questions.explain: Scientists look for evidence that microbial life may have existed in Mars's ancient environments.

questions.question: Which planet is often described as Earth's neighboring planet beyond Earth's orbit?
questions.explain: Mars is the next planet outward from Earth in the Solar System.
